- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening forecast slope.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–68), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion completes.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising or volatility is increasing.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment peaks; align forecast slope with sentiment direction, not just price history.
